title: English as a Foreign Language Instructors’ Professional Identity and Professional Development in Higher Education Institutions
authors: Hijjatul Qamariah
venue: SZTE Repository of Dissertations (University of Szeged)
abstract: Teacher Professional identity (TPI) and professional development (PD) are key constructs for the quality of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction in higher education. However, research in non Western contexts often lacks conceptual clarity and methodological depth in explaining how these constructs emerge and interact. Guided by a sociocultural perspective that views identity as socially constructed, negotiated, and shaped through participation in institutional practices, this study examines how Indonesian EFL instructors construct their professional identities and how these identities influence their teaching practice and engagement in professional development. An exploratory sequential mixed methods design was employed. The qualitative phase involved semi structured interviews (N = 10) and ego centered network cards (N = 11) to capture instructors’ lived experiences and the relational influences shaping their identities. Thematic analysis identified five themes: professional identity construction, professional development practices, pedagogical agency, institutional influence, emotional and relational dimensions. These themes informed the development of a survey instrument, which was validated and administered to 161 instructors across diverse higher education institutions. The quantitative phase used correlation analysis to examine associations among validated constructs: teaching practice, pedagogical knowledge, reflective practice, institutional support, and professional development. This was followed by multiple regression analyses to determine the extent to which TPI predicted these outcomes. The results showed strong correlations among all constructs. Multiple regression analysis showed that mentorship emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .473, p < .001), indicating that instructors who receive meaningful guidance and peer support tend to report stronger professional identities. Self directed learning also significantly predicted identity strength (β = .395, p < .001), suggesting that instructors who actively engage in autonomous learning and skill development tend to construct stronger professional identities. Institutional support also contributed significantly (β = .344, p < .001), demonstrating that supportive institutional contexts foster stronger professional identity formation. Teaching experience was not a significant predictor of professional identity (β = .026, p = .336), suggesting the accumulation of teaching experience alone does s not automatically result in a more developed professional identity. Regression analysis further showed that PI significantly predicted teaching practice and engagement in PD, suggesting that identity plays a substantial role in shaping professional behavior rather than merely reflecting accumulated experience. While professional development contributes to identity formation, the findings suggest that identity exerts a stronger influence on instructors’ developmental choices and instructional decisions, pointing to a reciprocal but asymmetrical relationship. This study contributes to the field in three main ways: (1) by offering a contextually grounded conceptualization of EFL instructor identity in Indonesian higher education; (2) by providing a validated measurement instrument that may support future research and policy-related work and (3) by presenting empirical evidence of the important role of identity in shaping teaching practice and sustained professional development. The findings underscore the importance of institutional environments that recognize the dynamic nature of teacher identity and provide meaningful, long term support for professional growth.

title: CON-SENSO. Reflections on Applied Anthropology On the Right to Health and Informed Consent
authors: Stefania Spada
venue: Directory of Open access Books (OAPEN Foundation)
abstract: Does informed consent truly guarantee a subjective, free, and informed right to health for everyone, without discrimination? In other words, does informed consent—as it is actually practiced—serve as a guarantor of rights? This paper will attempt to answer these questions by presenting the findings of an anthropological study conducted in the gynecology and obstetrics department of a university hospital in the Emilia-Romagna region. Drawing on philosophical and legal reflections, the author examines the capacity of fundamental rights—and in particular the right to health—to become substantive in the contemporary intercultural context. Enforceability in everyday practice must, in fact, be understood by considering the various dimensions of power that characterize relationships, first and foremost the doctor-patient relationship. Throughthe ethnography of healthcare practices, the ways in which informed consent is implemented engage in a dialogue with reflections on the critical issues and dysfunctions inherent in the corporate logic that structures the encounter between biomedical knowledge and citizens.

title: PhyAVBench: A Challenging Audio Physics-Sensitivity Benchmark for Physically Grounded Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
authors: Tianxin Xie; Wentao Lei; Kai Jiang; Guanjie Huang; Pengfei Zhang; Chunhui Zhang; Fengji Ma; Haoyu He; Han Zhang; Jiangshan He; Jinting Wang; Linghan Fang; Lufei Gao; Orkesh Ablet; Peihua Zhang; Ruolin Hu; Shengyu Li; Weilin Lin; Xiaoyang Feng; Xinyue Yang; Yan Rong; Yanyun Wang; Zihang Shao; Zelin Zhao; Chenxing Li; Shan Yang; Wenfu Wang; Meng Yu; Dong Yu; Li Liu
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
abstract: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation is central to applications such as filmmaking and world modeling. However, current models often fail to produce physically plausible sounds. Previous benchmarks primarily focus on audio-video temporal synchronization, while largely overlooking explicit evaluation of audio-physics grounding, thereby limiting the study of physically plausible audio-visual generation. To address this issue, we present PhyAVBench, the first benchmark that systematically evaluates the audio-physics grounding capabilities of T2AV, image-to-audio-video (I2AV), and video-to-audio (V2A) models. PhyAVBench offers PhyAV-Sound-11K, a new dataset of 25.5 hours of 11,605 audible videos collected from 184 participants to ensure diversity and avoid data leakage. It contains 337 paired-prompt groups with controlled physical variations that drive sound differences, each grounded with an average of 17 videos and spanning 6 audio-physics dimensions and 41 fine-grained test points. Each prompt pair is annotated with the physical factors underlying their acoustic differences. Importantly, PhyAVBench leverages paired text prompts to evaluate this capability. We term this evaluation paradigm the Audio-Physics Sensitivity Test (APST) and introduce a novel metric, the Contrastive Physical Response Score (CPRS), which quantifies the acoustic consistency between generated videos and their real-world counterparts. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 state-of-the-art models. Our results reveal that even leading commercial models struggle with fundamental audio-physical phenomena, exposing a critical gap beyond audio-visual synchronization and pointing to future research directions. We hope PhyAVBench will serve as a foundation for advancing physically grounded audio-visual generation. Prompts, ground-truth, and generated video samples are available at https://github.com/imxtx/PhyAVBench.

title: Robust Mesh Saliency Ground Truth Acquisition in VR via View Cone Sampling and Manifold Diffusion
authors: Guoquan Zheng; Jie Hao; Yongming M Han; Liang Yuan; Huiyu Duan; Long Tang; Shuo Yang; Yucheng Zhu; Patrick Le Callet
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
abstract: As the complexity of 3D digital content grows exponentially, understanding human visual attention is critical for optimizing rendering and processing resources. Therefore, reliable 3D mesh saliency ground truth (GT) is essential for human-centric visual modeling in virtual reality (VR). However, existing VR eye-tracking frameworks are fundamentally bottlenecked by their underlying acquisition and generation mechanisms. The reliance on zero-area single ray sampling (SRS) fails to capture contextual features, leading to severe texture aliasing and discontinuous saliency signals. And the conventional application of Euclidean smoothing propagates saliency across disconnected physical gaps, resulting in semantic confusion on complex 3D manifolds. This paper proposes a robust framework to address these limitations. We first introduce a view cone sampling (VCS) strategy, which simulates the human foveal receptive field via Gaussian-distributed ray bundles to improve sampling robustness for complex topologies. Furthermore, a hybrid Manifold-Euclidean constrained diffusion (HCD) algorithm is developed, fusing manifold geodesic constraints with Euclidean scales to ensure topologically-consistent saliency propagation. We demonstrate the improvement in performance over baseline methods and the benefits for downstream tasks through subjective experiments and qualitative and quantitative methods. By mitigating "topological short-circuits" and aliasing, our framework provides a high-fidelity 3D attention acquisition paradigm that aligns with natural human perception, offering a more accurate and robust baseline for 3D mesh saliency research.

title: MM-OpenFGL: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Federated Graph Learning
authors: Xunkai Li; Yuming Ai; Yinlin Zhu; Haodong Lu; Yi Zhang; Guohao Fu; Bowen Fan; Ronghua Li; Guoren Wang
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
abstract: Multimodal-attributed graphs (MMAGs) provide a unified framework for modeling complex relational data by integrating heterogeneous modalities with graph structures. While centralized learning has shown promising performance, MMAGs in real-world applications are often distributed across isolated platforms and cannot be shared due to privacy concerns or commercial constraints. Federated graph learning (FGL) offers a natural solution for collaborative training under such settings; however, existing studies largely focus on single-modality graphs and do not adequately address the challenges unique to multimodal federated graph learning (MMFGL). To bridge this gap, we present MM-OpenFGL, the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically formalizes the MMFGL paradigm and enables rigorous evaluation. MM-OpenFGL comprises 19 multimodal datasets spanning 7 application domains, 8 simulation strategies capturing modality and topology variations, 6 downstream tasks, and 57 state-of-the-art methods implemented through a modular API. Extensive experiments investigate MMFGL from the perspectives of necessity, effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency, offering valuable insights for future research on MMFGL.

title: Self-evolving Embodied AI
authors: Tongtong Feng; Xin Eric Wang; Wenwu Zhu
abstract: Abstract Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an intelligent system formed by agents and their environment through active perception, embodied cognition, and action interaction. Existing embodied AI remains confined to human-crafted setting, in which agents are trained on given memories and construct models for given tasks, enabling fixed physical embodiments to interact with relatively static environments. Such methods fail in in-the-wild setting characterized by variable physical embodiments and dynamic open environments. This paper introduces self-evolving embodied AI, a new paradigm in which agents operate based on their changing physical embodiment and environment through five software-level components, namely memory self-updating, task self-switching, environment self-prediction, embodiment self-adaptation, and model self-evolution, together with a hardware-level component for physical embodiment evolution, aiming to achieve continually adaptive intelligence through software-hardware co-evolution. Specifically, we present the definition, framework, components, mechanisms, roadmap, and evaluation indicators of self-evolving embodied AI, systematically review state-of-the-art works for realized components, discuss practical applications, and point out future research directions. We believe that self-evolving embodied AI enables agents to autonomously learn and interact with environments in a human-like manner and provides a new perspective toward general artificial intelligence.

title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
authors: Arpit Bahety; Skand Peri; Sriniket Ambatipudi; Chen Xu; Haruki Nishimura; Masha Itkina; Roberto Martín-Martín
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

title: WAM-Sim0.1: World Anchored Memory Meets Online RL for Consistent and Realistic Driving Simulation
authors: Jiahao Cui; Jiaye Li; Wenhao Zhang; Yaoyi Li; Shan Luan; Quanhui Tang; Jianhua Han; Lin Cheng; Hang Xu; Siyu Zhu
abstract: Autoregressive driving world models systematically suffer from structural drift, identity drift, and quality decay over long rollout horizons due to transient conditioning signals that lack persistent state. We present WAM-Sim, a driving world model anchored by a persistent hierarchical memory and optimized via online flow-matching RL. WAM-Sim structures persistent context across three temporal and semantic scales: pose-aligned structural tokens encoding persistent road topology, read-only scene tokens supplying geolocated background appearance, and write-once instance tokens preserving individual traffic participant identities across occlusions and chunk boundaries. To restore visual sharpness and physical plausibility degraded by multi-scale conditioning, we introduce an online post-training framework that optimizes self-generated rollouts via flow-matching RL guided by hierarchy-aligned visual rewards and a vision-language model physical judge. The invariant memory empirically confines policy optimization within the anchored context, helping suppress semantic collapse and reward hacking, while online RL systematically enforces physical commonsense and fine-grained visual fidelity. On the nuScenes benchmark, WAM-Sim achieves a superior generation fidelity (FID=3.47, FVD=25.72) and strong downstream perception performance (24.16 mAP, 71.23 road mIoU). On minute-scale rollouts of self-collected data, WAM-Sim substantially mitigates structural and identity drift, preserving high scene similarity and subject identity coherence across extended horizons. Project page: https://fudan-generative-vision.github.io/WAM-Sim.

title: Bridging Structure and Semantics: Knowledge Graph Verification via Triple-to-Text Alignment
authors: Ziang Cui
abstract: Semantic accuracy is an important dimension of knowledge graph quality. Graph-based scoring methods exploit relational structure, while textual representations allow classifiers to draw on knowledge encoded by pre-trained language models (PLMs). We present GenVer, a generative verifier that scores triples using both their serialized form and generated natural language representations (NLRs). A triple-text alignment procedure selects training pairs for a sequence-to-sequence generator; a BERT-based classifier then combines features from each triple and its generated NLR. On four FactFB variants, constructed from FB15k using perturbed negative triples, GenVer obtains the highest classification accuracy among the evaluated baselines, ranging from 88.56% to 91.52%. The experiments suggest that generated representations can help triple classification, while the case analysis also exposes semantic drift and high-confidence errors.

title: Multimodal Information Interactions Bottleneck for Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning
authors: Liangjian Wen; Jiangtao Zheng; Jiang Duan; Qun Dai; Yong Dai; Jianzhuang Liu; Jun Wang; Shu-Dong Huang; Xinwang Liu; Zenglin Xu; Zhao Kang
abstract: Multimodal self-supervised learning is challenged by heterogeneity, unequal informativeness, and complex information interactions across multimodal data sources such as images, text, audio, and tabular data. While contrastive methods effectively align shared semantics, they typically rely on strong multi-view redundancy assumptions, overlooking modality-specific and synergistic information, thus leading to suboptimal representations. We propose the Multimodal Information Interactions Bottleneck (MIIB), a principled framework grounded in Partial Information Decomposition that explicitly encodes redundant, unique, and synergistic information within multimodal interactions. MIIB employs a dual-path model architecture for modality-specific encoding and multimodal fusion, optimized using surrogate tractable entropy-based objectives that enforce minimal sufficient representations without requiring explicit mutual information estimation. By leveraging variational bounds and score-based entropy estimation, MIIB efficiently captures complex cross-modal interactions while suppressing superfluous information. Experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art multimodal self-supervised methods. Code is available at https://github.com/wanglingzaishi/MIIB.

title: TRACEMARK: Editor-Aware Watermarking for User Attribution in Text-Guided Image Editing
authors: Xiaodong Wu; Xiangman Li; Jianbing Ni; Rongxing Lu
abstract: An image editing service records which user requests each edit, but the edited image itself does not contain this account information. Once the image is downloaded and shared, the service cannot identify the requesting user from the image alone. Embedding a user-specific watermark could enable such attribution, but semantic editing may erase the signal. We propose Tracemark, an editor-aware watermarking framework for identifying users from edited images. A shared encoder embeds a user-specific signal before editing, and a shared detector recovers the user by comparing features of the edited image with learned reference vectors. Both components are trained jointly through an editor with fixed parameters. User identification errors encourage the encoder to produce watermarks that survive editing, while fidelity losses limit changes to the input image and intended edit. Each image domain and editing instruction uses a separately trained model shared across registered users. Experiments on three image domains show that editor-aware training improves user recovery with both reference-vector matching and binary watermark decoding. Separately trained models reach 87.5% mean identification accuracy among 500 users. When tested with a different editor without retraining, the watermark modules still recover user information. These results demonstrate that learning watermarks through the editing process enables user attribution without modifying the editor.

title: FUSEMOS: Perceptual Evaluation of Text-to-Music Generation with Dual-Encoder Fusion and Ranking-Aware Composite Loss
authors: Jing Yang; Haoyu Wang; Ningning Pan; Zhao Wang; Jianxuan Yang; Gongping Huang
abstract: Perceptual evaluation of generated music is essential for developing text-to-music (TTM) generation systems. Existing automatic music perceptual evaluation methods rely solely on the contrastive language audio pretraining (CLAP) model to extract both audio and text features for predicting human-annotated mean opinion scores (MOS), particularly for overall musical impression (OMI) and textual alignment (TA). However, CLAP is limited in capturing fine-grained musical attributes such as timbre and expressiveness \emph{etc}. To address this, we propose FUSEMOS, a dual-encoder fusion framework that integrates CLAP with MERT, a self-supervised model pretrained on large scale music audio, to better capture both high level semantic alignment and detailed musical characteristics for more accurate OMI and TA estimation. Furthermore, to overcome the limitations of conventional regression losses in measuring human preferred relative ranking of music segments, we design a novel ranking-aware composite loss function. Experiments conducted on the MusicEval benchmark demonstrate that our approach outperforms the existing SOTA methods in both mean squared error and rank correlation metrics by a large margin.

title: OptST: Optimizing Semantic Tokenization for LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
authors: Hanchong Chen; Jie Liu; Fuyuan Lyu; Dugang Liu; Lingjie Li; Xiuqiang He; Xing Tang
abstract: Semantic information can enrich the identifiers and structured fields used by recommender systems. Semantic tokenization provides a structured representation of this information by converting LLM-derived user profiles into discrete tokens. In the common two-stage pipeline, the tokenizer is trained before the recommender. Its token assignments are then treated as fixed input features during recommendation training. As a result, the downstream recommender can learn how to use the assigned indices, but it cannot revise the semantic partition that produced them. Making this partition task-aware is difficult because nearest-code assignment is discrete, and unconstrained adaptation may also distort the geometry learned during pretraining. Moreover, a fixed token depth exposes the same semantic resolution to every interaction. We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different recommendation backbones. These results establish task-aware semantic tokenization as an effective interface between LLM-derived profiles and downstream recommendation models.

title: A Unified Multi-Encoder Framework for Music Lyric Intelligibility Assessment: Bridging Invasive and Non-Invasive Paradigms
authors: Jing Yang; Shenghao Liao; Shuqing Zhang; Yongyi Deng; Pan Li; Zerui Han; Gongping Huang
abstract: Lyric intelligibility significantly impacts music engagement and comprehension, especially for hearing-impaired individuals. Existing speech intelligibility metrics perform poorly in musical contexts due to differences in prosody, timing, and spectral dynamics. We propose a unified multi-encoder framework that supports both invasive and non-invasive modeling for robust lyric intelligibility prediction. By capturing complementary local acoustic-semantic alignments, global musical semantics, and ASR-derived textual cues, our method achieves superior performance over baselines on the ICASSP 2026 Cadenza dataset, with the best model achieving 26.61 RMSE, a $9.2$\% improvement over the baseline, demonstrating its flexibility and robustness.

title: TICK: Text-Informed Contrastive Kernels for Probabilistic Time-Series Retrieval
authors: Rayen Ben Masseoud; Faïcel Chamroukhi
abstract: The coexistence of sensor data and textual knowledge across industrialapplications highlights the need to align natural language withmultivariate time series. This challenge is typically treated as adeterministic task, ignoring the fact that a vague query may matchhundreds of recordings while a precise one matches only a few. We arguethat text-to-time-series retrieval is inherently a probabilisticcross-modal problem and propose TICK, a framework in which each textquery carries a learned uncertainty $\sigma_t$ reflecting how many timeseries are semantically compatible with it. Without supervising $\sigma_t$directly, we find that it tracks query specificity with Spearmancorrelations $\rho \in [-0.88, -0.75]$ on three independent industrialbenchmarks. We further show that coupling the time-series representationto the text query is a necessary condition for this calibration to emerge:without it, $\sigma_t$ collapses to a constant, eliminating the model'sability to adapt its retrieval scope to query specificity. Because$\sigma_t$ sets the retrieval scope of a query, TICK spends a query-dependentcandidate budget instead of a fixed worst-case one, on top of a frozen33M-parameter sentence encoder and a small patch Transformer, with no languagemodel in the inference loop.

title: Funkční přípustkové konstrukce v češtině a francouzštině: kontrastivní korpusová studie
authors: Ondřej Drobník
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: This paper investigates concessive constructions in Czech and French, focusing on so-called functional concessives—expressions where concessive meaning arises not from explicit grammatical markers but from semantic-pragmatic configurations. The theoretical foundation is the “concessive triangle,” a ternary model based on the disruption of expected inference; although premise P holds, the anticipated consequence Q does not follow (non-Q). Adopting a maximalist perspective, the study classifies concessive constructions under three categories: formal, mixed, and functional, the last being central to the analysis. Drawing on data from the InterCorp parallel corpus, the study proposes a typology of functional categories (e.g., contradiction, alternative, totality, irrelevance) and shows how concessivity can be lexically encoded or contextually inferred. The framework of Construction Grammar allows for a unified treatment of form–function pairings across both canonical and peripheral realizations. The results highlight the cross-linguistic diversity of concessive strategies and offer a new descriptive and theoretical model for future contrastive and corpusbased research.

title: Evaluating embeddings for one-shot classification of doctor-AI consultations
authors: Olumide Ebenezer Ojo; Olaronke Oluwayemisi Adebanji; Consuelo V. García-Mendoza; Alexander Gelbukh; Hiram Calvo; Anna Feldman
abstract: Effective communication between healthcare providers and patients is crucial to providing high-quality patient care. In this work, we investigate how Doctor-written and AI-generated texts in healthcare consultations can be classified using state-of-the-art embeddings and one-shot classification systems. By analyzing embeddings such as bag-of-words, character n-grams, Word2Vec, GloVe, fastText, and GPT2 embeddings, we examine how well our one-shot classification systems capture semantic information within medical consultations. Results show that the embeddings are capable of capturing semantic features from text in a reliable and adaptable manner. Overall, Word2Vec, GloVe and Character n-grams embeddings performed well, indicating their suitability for modeling targeted to this task. GPT2 embedding also shows notable performance, indicating its suitability for models tailored to this task as well. Our machine learning architectures significantly improved the quality of health conversations when training data are scarce, improving communication between patients and healthcare providers.

title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
authors: Efthymios Georgiou; Ioannis Kakogeorgiou; Sarah Brüningk
abstract: Transfer learning from natural images is standard in supervised and increasingly adopted in self-supervised medical image analysis, but its role in generative modelling, and in particular diffusion denoisers, remains underexplored. Medical diffusion models typically train the denoiser from scratch, with no systematic evaluation of natural-image transfer. We analyse this across latent and pixel paradigms, model sizes (131M-952M) and two radiology datasets (RadImageNet, BraTS), and ask which aspects of transfer support generation. We find that: i) Natural-image initialisation consistently improves generation, by 21-34% relative gFID in pixel space against 14% in latent space, where the tokeniser supplies much of the prior. gFID gains mirror downstream pathology classification and radiomic-feature FD, both proxies for clinical fidelity. ii) Benefits reflect spatial structure, not semantics: semantic probing does not predict generation quality, whereas a spatial-structure metric adapted to internal denoiser representations tracks gFID at $|r|=0.85$, positioning spatial organisation as a channel through which pretraining manifests. iii) Mixed-domain denoiser training shows that natural and medical images share similar layer-wise representations up to the late blocks, and mixing natural images into medical training improves fidelity. iv) Transfer benefit is tied to natural image initialisation, outperforming in-domain medical pretraining and several reinitialisation schemes. Overall, natural image denoisers transfer positively to medical ones in our setup. Code is available at https://github.com/CAIROLab-Bern/rad-dit

title: Flat Features, Detailed Images? Simple Detail Control for Diffusion Transformers
authors: Qingtao Yu; Zhen Wang; Jiyang Zheng; Minghao Sun; Hongdong Li; Dylan Campbell
abstract: Prompt engineering is commonly used to encourage text-to-image models to generate more detailed images. However, it does not provide reliable, continuous, or disentangled control. We analyze feature tokens produced with and without detail-enhancing prompts across six diffusion transformers and observe a common pattern: these prompts tend to increase the entropy of each token's energy distribution while largely preserving its ordering. That is, flattening the distribution increases the level of detail. Motivated by this counter-intuitive finding, we introduce a simple training-free approach that continuously adjusts the level of detail according to a scalar. Specifically, it shifts the squared channel magnitudes of each token toward a higher entropy distribution with a time-aware scheduler to concentrate the intervention at intermediate sampling steps. Across extensive experiments on different types of diffusion transformers, we show that our approach provides continuous control over detail metrics while largely preserving image quality and semantic structure. It requires only a few lines of code and adds negligible inference time overhead.

title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
authors: Haoqing Wang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Sicheng Fan; Zhexin Zhang; Xinjie Zhang; Jiahao Li; Bin Li; Yan Lu
abstract: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle tasks ranging from everyday desktop activities to long-horizon professional workflows. Yet interfaces centered on screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions can impose a human-interaction prior, requiring repeated screen interpretation while leaving the computer's semantic and programmatic capabilities underexposed. We argue for exposing these capabilities and letting models choose and combine them. We introduce Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), a unified interface for general agents that combines three complementary channels: programmatic interaction through code and command-line tools, semantic interaction through accessibility (AX), and visual interaction through graphical user interfaces (GUI). Our HCU supports efficient AX interaction and guards against stale-state actions during channel switching. A supplementary HCU skill guides agents in selecting and coordinating channels to use the unified interface effectively. Our designed AX tools return compact observations, execute actions in batches, and report their effects as AX diffs, so the model needs fewer round trips. On OSWorld 2.0, HCU achieves the highest Partial and Binary scores among the compared systems. Analyzing agent trajectories, we find that all evaluated models improve with HCU yet allocate work across the channels differently and consistently outperform compared baselines in terms of both efficiency and task success, highlighting the value of unified computer-use interfaces that allow flexible channel selection and combination.

title: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version)
authors: Jens Sprengers; Marton Bognar; Lesly-Ann Daniel; Frank Piessens
abstract: Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a microarchitectural optimization recently introduced in mainstream desktop and server CPUs. Although DMPs offer performance improvements, they have been shown to enable side-channel leakage of secrets, even from constant-time code that has been hardened against Spectre attacks. Unfortunately, existing defenses either incur significant performance overhead or, as we show, fail to prevent all DMP leakage. In this work, we address this gap by designing a defense that is both secure and efficient. First, we propose a classification of DMP leakage, categorize existing and novel attacks, and analyze which leakage classes are mitigated by existing defenses. We validate this analysis empirically by implementing the first open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor, showing that the only existing defense that aims to preserve DMP performance fails to protect against entire leakage classes. Next, we propose SecDMP, a provably secure and efficient hardware-based defense. SecDMP requires secrets to be marked in memory and ensures that DMPs never encode these secrets in the microarchitecture---without compromising performance for public data. We formally prove that SecDMP introduces no leakage beyond a baseline semantics without DMPs. Notably, when combined with speculative-execution defenses, SecDMP restores complete microarchitectural security for constant-time code. Finally, our empirical evaluation shows that SecDMP prevents all DMP leakage while incurring minimal performance overhead and hardware cost.

title: Computational Studies of Triplet State Formation in Zinc Dipyrrin Complexes
authors: Reuben Kwabla Adigbli
venue: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
abstract: Zinc dipyrromethene complexes are promising earth-abundant photosensitizers due to their strong visible-light absorption and tunable excited states. To rationally design them for photocatalysis and photodynamic therapy, a molecular-level understanding of triplet-state formation is needed, but details of intersystem crossing remain unclear. To study the effect of π-extension, we synthesized an indole-substituted zinc dipyrrin complex: the dipyrromethane ligand was prepared from indole and mesitaldehyde, oxidized to the dipyrromethene, then coordinated with zinc. DFT and TD-DFT calculations determined ground and excited-state geometries and energies in different solvents, modeled absorption spectra, and visualized charge distributions. The results show how solvent polarity shifts energies of the ground, lowest triplet, and excited singlet states, and influences charge separation in the excited state. These computational findings, coupled with photophysical measurements, will establish a framework for designing zinc dipyrrin complexes with improved triplet state yield.

title: On the Reuse Practices in GitHub Actions Workflows
authors: Hassan Onsori Delicheh
abstract: Automation is fundamental to modern software engineering, with platforms such as GitHub providing built-in systems like GitHub Actions to streamline tasks across the software development lifecycle. Similar to traditional open-source software reuse, automated workflows rely heavily on reusable components such as Actions and reusable workflows. While this reliance offers significant productivity benefits, it also introduces critical dependency-related risks within the software supply chain, particularly regarding security vulnerabilities and maintainability. To address these overlooked challenges, this PhD dissertation presents a comprehensive empirical investigation into automation and reuse practices within the GitHub Actions ecosystem. Employing a mixed-methods approach, it combines qualitative survey findings from workflow practitioners with large-scale software repository mining. Through this empirical lens, the research evaluates workflow reuse behaviours, quantifies component outdatedness, maps complex dependency networks, and assesses ecosystem-wide security dimensions. The findings reveal key motivations and selection criteria behind workflow reuse while uncovering widespread vulnerability exposure and maintenance challenges. Ultimately, this work provides actionable guidance and insights for practitioners, tool developers, and researchers to foster a more secure, reliable, and maintainable workflow automation ecosystem.
